threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success criteria, and responsibilities for the framework project.

messages.text:
Good morning team. We're kicking off the Design and Rollout of Inclusive Hiring and Onboarding Framework project today. The goal is to create a standardized, inclusive hiring and onboarding process across all business units within 30 days. This ties directly to our compliance obligations and retention goals.

Key deliverables: end-to-end process map (A1), standardized job posting and interview toolkit (A4), inclusive hiring guidelines (A2), onboarding checklist with 90-day plan (A3), and KPI dashboard definition (A5).

I want to confirm scope with everyone: are we including all business units in the initial rollout, or are we piloting first? Also, let's clarify role ownership for T1 (process mapping), T6 (KPI definition), and the overall governance structure. Thoughts?

Thanks for the clear framing. I'd recommend we pilot first with one business unit before full rollout—that way we can test the process, gather feedback, and adjust before scaling. Reduces risk of adoption issues and gives us real data on time-to-hire impact.

For scope: I think we should include all major hiring workflows (permanent, fixed-term, internal transfers) but exclude contractor/agency hiring for now. That can be a phase 2 if needed.

On roles: I can own T1 (process mapping) and coordinate with the team on validating current state across units. Who's taking the lead on T6 (KPI definition)?

Pilot approach makes sense—aligns with our risk mitigation strategy. Scope sounds right: permanent, fixed-term, internal transfers in scope; contractors out for now.

For T6, I'll take ownership on the KPI definition. I want to ensure we're tracking not just speed (time-to-hire) but also quality metrics—offer acceptance rate, 90-day retention, and diversity indicators. We'll need to align with payroll and HRIS on data availability, so T5 (payroll/HRIS alignment) becomes a dependency.

Let me propose: 441030 owns T1, I own T6 and T5. We need someone to drive T2 (job posting templates) and T3 (anti-bias guidelines). Who's available?

I can take T2 (job posting and interview templates). I've worked on recruitment campaigns before and understand what makes a posting inclusive and clear. I'll draft templates with examples of good language and what to avoid.

Question: should the templates include specific accommodations language for candidates with disabilities, or is that covered separately in the anti-bias guideline?

Good question. Both. The job posting template (T2) should include a standard line inviting candidates to request accommodations. The anti-bias guideline (T3) will go deeper—concrete examples of what accommodations we can offer, how to respond to requests, and how to avoid screening out candidates based on disability status.

I'll own T3 since it touches on labour legislation and compliance. I want to make sure we're aligned with employment law across all regions we operate in.

So: 441030 → T1, 549423 → T2, me → T3 and T6 and T5. That leaves T4 (onboarding checklist), T7 (manager training), T8 (pilot execution), T9 (feedback collection), T10 (post-pilot updates), T11 (escalation path), T12 (governance). Who wants to step up on the onboarding side?

I can take T4 (onboarding checklist and 90-day plan). I've been through onboarding processes from both sides and know what works and what gets missed. I'll make sure it covers pre-boarding, first week, first month, and 90-day touchpoints, including specific steps for remote hires and people with disabilities.

I'll need feedback from at least one business unit manager and one HR manager to validate, as per the definition of done. Should I start drafting this week?

Yes, start this week. Once you have a draft, I can review from a manager's perspective—I've hired several people recently and can give you real feedback on what's practical.

For T7 (manager training) and T8 (pilot execution), I think those should go together. We need to train managers on the new process before we pilot. I can coordinate the pilot with a business unit—I have a good relationship with the Operations team. They're hiring for three roles in the next month, so timing works.

Who takes T7 and T9 (feedback collection)?

I can help with T7 (manager training). I can work with 549423 or whoever's leading the templates to create a simple training deck and quick reference guide. Managers are busy, so we need to keep it short and practical.

For T9 (feedback collection), I think that should be someone who can gather honest feedback without managers feeling like they're being evaluated. Maybe 549423 or 167595 could do that?

I can take T9 (feedback collection). I'll prepare a survey and interview script to gather input from candidates, new hires, and managers after the pilot. I'll aim for at least 10 responses and summarize key themes and improvement suggestions.

So to recap the ownership:
- 441030: T1 (process mapping), T8 (pilot execution)
- 549423: T2 (templates), T9 (feedback collection)
- 17956: T3 (anti-bias guideline), T5 (payroll/HRIS alignment), T6 (KPI definition)
- 167595: T4 (onboarding checklist)
- 552174: T7 (manager training)

Who's taking T10 (post-pilot updates), T11 (escalation path), T12 (governance)?

I'll take T10 (post-pilot updates) and T12 (governance). Those are strategic and need to align with compliance and long-term maintenance. T11 (escalation path) should go to someone who understands day-to-day HR operations—maybe 82204 or 552174?

I can take T11 (escalation path). I'll document common issue types and create a simple flow so the team knows who to contact for different problems. I'll validate contact points with everyone once it's drafted.

Great. So on scope: we're piloting first with one business unit (Operations), then rolling out to all units. We're including permanent, fixed-term, and internal transfers. Contractors are out of scope for now.

Role ownership is clear. Timeline: we have 30 days total. I'd suggest we aim to have all drafts ready by day 10, pilot running by day 15, feedback collected by day 25, and final updates by day 28. Does that feel realistic?

Timeline is tight but doable if we move fast. One thing I want to flag: we need legal review on T2 (templates) and T3 (guidelines) before pilot. That's a dependency I can't skip. I'll coordinate with legal, but we need to build that into the schedule.

Also, T5 (payroll/HRIS alignment) needs to happen early so we know if there are any system constraints. I'll reach out to the payroll team this week.

Let's lock in: D1 (scope) and D2 (role ownership) are confirmed as of now. Next step: everyone starts drafting their assigned tasks. Daily async check-in on blockers. Sound good?
Agreed. I'll start on T2 templates today. Quick question: do we have any existing job posting templates or interview guides I should build from, or am I starting from scratch?

We have some old templates floating around, but they're not standardized. I'll send you what I have, but honestly, starting fresh with best practices is probably better. Focus on inclusive language, clear role requirements, and structured interview questions. That's what we need.
I'll start on T4 (onboarding checklist) this week too. I'll draft something by end of week and share for feedback. 441030, can you review from a manager's lens once I have something?
Absolutely. Send it over and I'll turn around feedback quickly. I want to make sure it's not too heavy for busy managers.

Alright, team. Let's confirm the decisions we've made today:

D1: Scope is permanent, fixed-term, and internal transfer hiring. Contractors out of scope for now. Pilot first with one business unit (Operations), then full rollout.

D2: Role ownership assigned as follows:
- 441030: T1 (process mapping), T8 (pilot execution)
- 549423: T2 (job posting templates), T9 (feedback collection)
- 17956: T3 (anti-bias guideline), T5 (payroll/HRIS alignment), T6 (KPI definition), T10 (post-pilot updates), T12 (governance)
- 167595: T4 (onboarding checklist)
- 552174: T7 (manager training)
- 82204: T11 (escalation path)

Next steps: everyone starts drafting this week. Daily async updates on blockers. Legal review needed for T2 and T3 before pilot. Payroll/HRIS check on T5 this week.

Let's move fast and stay aligned. I'll post a weekly summary every Friday with decisions, risks, and next steps.

threads.thread_goal: Define and validate standardized hiring templates and inclusive guidelines.

messages.text:
Hi team, I've drafted the job posting and interview toolkit (A4) and wanted to share for feedback. The toolkit includes:

1. Job posting template with inclusive language guidelines (e.g., 'we welcome applications from people of all backgrounds', clear accessibility statement)
2. Structured interview guide with behavioral and technical questions
3. Interview scorecard to reduce bias in evaluation

I've included examples of what to do and what to avoid. The template is designed to be simple enough for any manager to use, not just HR.

Please review and let me know if anything needs adjustment. I know 17956 and I need to get legal sign-off on this before we use it in the pilot.

Thanks for getting this out quickly. I reviewed the draft and it looks solid. The job posting template is clear and the interview scorecard is practical. One thing: the scorecard has a lot of fields. Will managers actually fill all of it out, or should we simplify?

Good point. I can trim it down to the essentials: candidate name, role, date, five key competencies with a 1-5 rating, and a final recommendation. That's cleaner and still captures what we need to reduce bias.

I've reviewed the templates from a compliance angle. The inclusive language is good, but I want to strengthen the accessibility statement. Instead of just 'we welcome applications', let's add a specific line: 'If you need accommodations during the application or interview process, please let us know and we will work with you to provide them.'

Also, the interview guide needs a note that interviewers should not ask about disability status, family plans, or other protected characteristics. I'll add that and send back a revised version for your review.

Once we align on the language, I'll send to legal for formal sign-off. Timeline: I can have legal review by end of this week.

Perfect. I like the stronger accessibility language. And yes, the note on protected characteristics is important—I should have been more explicit about that. Let me incorporate your changes and send back by tomorrow.
Quick question: does the job posting template include a line about remote work options or flexibility? We've had candidates ask about that, and it affects their decision to apply.

Good catch. I have a section for 'Work Arrangements' but it's optional. I'll make it a standard field so every posting includes it. That way candidates know upfront if a role is remote, hybrid, or on-site.

I'm also working on T3 (the inclusive hiring and anti-bias guideline, A2). This will be the companion document to the templates. It covers:

1. Bias awareness: unconscious bias, how it shows up in hiring, and how to mitigate it
2. Disability accommodations: concrete examples of what we can offer (flexible interview times, written questions in advance, accessible interview space, etc.)
3. Gender equality: ensuring job descriptions don't use gendered language, and that we're actively recruiting from diverse talent pools

I'll have a draft by end of week and will send to legal along with the templates. Both documents need to be approved together since they're interdependent.

This is important. I've seen hiring decisions that didn't follow best practices, so having clear guidelines will help. One thing to include: what happens if a manager doesn't follow the guidelines? Is there a consequence, or is it just guidance?

Good question. The guideline will frame it as a requirement, not just guidance. We'll include a section on governance and accountability—managers are responsible for following the process, and HR will audit a sample of hiring decisions to ensure compliance. Non-compliance could trigger retraining or escalation depending on severity. I'll detail that in the governance document (T12) as well.
So to confirm: once 17956 gets legal sign-off on both A4 (templates) and A2 (guidelines), we can move forward with D3 and D4? Or do we need another round of review?

Once legal signs off, I'll bring both documents back to the team for final approval. I want 441030 to review from a manager's perspective one more time, and 549423 to confirm the templates are still practical. Then we can lock in D3 (approve templates for pilot) and D4 (sign off on guidelines).

Target: legal review by end of this week, team review next Monday, decisions locked by Tuesday. That keeps us on track for pilot launch mid-project.

next_steps.when: legal review by end of week

threads.thread_goal: Finalize onboarding checklist, 90-day plan, and integration with payroll/HRIS.

messages.text:
Hi team, I've drafted the onboarding checklist and 90-day integration plan (A3). The checklist covers:

- Pre-boarding: offer acceptance, background check, equipment setup
- First week: welcome meeting, system access, team introductions, first-day checklist
- First month: role-specific training, manager check-in, HR orientation
- 90 days: performance review, feedback collection, retention decision

I've included specific steps for remote hires (e.g., virtual welcome, equipment shipped in advance) and people with disabilities (e.g., accessibility setup, accommodation check-ins).

I need feedback on feasibility from a manager's perspective (441030) and from HR (17956). Is this too heavy, or does it feel right?
I like the structure. One concern: the first-week checklist has about 15 items. That's a lot for a new hire's first day. Can we prioritize? Maybe 'must do on day 1' vs. 'should do by end of week'?
Good point. I'll reorganize it: day 1 essentials (welcome, system access, safety/compliance), then days 2-5 (team meetings, role training, etc.). That spreads it out and makes it less overwhelming.

I reviewed the checklist and it looks comprehensive. One thing I want to flag: the 90-day review step needs to tie into payroll and HRIS. We need to make sure the new hire is fully set up in both systems before day 1, and the 90-day review needs to trigger any probation-end actions in HRIS.

That's part of T5 (payroll/HRIS alignment). I've started that conversation with the payroll team. Initial feedback: they can handle most of this with existing processes, but we need to document the exact touchpoints and timing.

I'll send you a draft of the HRIS/payroll integration map by end of week. Can you review it and confirm the checklist aligns?
Yes, absolutely. Send me the integration map and I'll adjust the checklist to match. I want to make sure we're not creating manual workarounds if HRIS can handle it automatically.
Quick question on the accessibility setup step: what does that look like in practice? Do we have a standard list of accommodations we offer, or is it case-by-case?

That's covered in the anti-bias guideline (A2, T3). We'll have a standard list of common accommodations (ergonomic equipment, software licenses, flexible hours, etc.) and a process for requesting additional accommodations. The onboarding checklist should reference that guideline and include a step: 'Ask new hire if they need any accommodations and process request through HR.'
Got it. I'll add that step to the checklist. So the flow is: during onboarding, manager asks about accommodations, new hire can request, and HR processes it. That's clear.
One more thing: the 90-day review. Is that a formal performance review, or just a check-in? And who owns it—the manager or HR?

It's a structured check-in, not a formal performance review. The manager leads it with the new hire, and HR provides a template. It covers: role fit, learning progress, any issues or concerns, and a decision on whether to move forward (which triggers the probation-end action in HRIS). HR should follow up with the manager to ensure it's completed.

That works. I'll make sure the HRIS integration map includes the 90-day trigger. So the timeline is:

- Day 1: new hire fully set up in HRIS and payroll
- Day 30: first manager check-in (documented in checklist)
- Day 90: formal check-in and probation-end decision (triggers HRIS update)

I'll have the integration map ready by end of week. Once you confirm alignment, we can move to D5 (approve onboarding checklist for pilot) and D6 (agree on payroll/HRIS changes).
Sounds good. I'll wait for your integration map and then finalize the checklist. Target: I'll have the final version ready for approval by next Monday.
I'll review the final checklist once it's ready. I want to make sure it's practical for a busy manager. If it looks good, I can sign off on D5.

Perfect. I'll send the integration map to 167595 by EOD tomorrow. Once that's reviewed and the checklist is finalized, we'll have everything we need for D5 and D6. Let's aim for final approval by Tuesday so we can move into pilot planning.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and monitor the pilot, including training and communication to managers.

messages.text:
Team, I've confirmed with the Operations business unit that they're ready to pilot the new hiring framework. They have three open roles (two permanent, one fixed-term) and are planning to hire over the next 4 weeks. Perfect timing.

Proposed pilot timeline:
- Week 1 (this week): finalize all templates and guidelines, train Operations managers
- Week 2: start recruiting using new process
- Week 3-4: conduct interviews, make offers, onboard new hires
- Week 5: collect feedback from candidates, managers, and new hires

I'll coordinate with the Operations manager (external stakeholder) to ensure they're aligned. We'll need the manager training (T7) and communication pack (A6) ready by end of this week. Who's leading that?

I'm on it. I'm working with 549423 on the training deck. We're keeping it short: 30-minute overview of the new process, walkthrough of the templates, and a Q&A. I'll also create a one-page quick reference guide that managers can keep at their desk.

I'll have a draft by Thursday. Can someone review it before we deliver to Operations?
I'll review it Thursday and give feedback. I want to make sure it's clear and doesn't overwhelm the managers. They're busy and need to understand the 'why' and the 'how' quickly.

Good. I want to add one thing to the training: a section on compliance and anti-bias. Managers need to understand that this isn't just a process change—it's about legal compliance and fairness. I'll draft a 5-minute segment on that and send to 552174 by Wednesday.
Perfect. I'll incorporate that. So the training will be: overview of new process, templates walkthrough, compliance/anti-bias segment, Q&A, and quick reference guide. That should cover it.
I'll make sure the templates are finalized and ready to share with Operations by Friday. Once they have the templates and training, they can start using the new process for their open roles.

Great. So D7 (select pilot business unit and timeframe) is locked: Operations, 4-week pilot starting next week. D8 (approve manager training plan) will be confirmed once 552174 and I review the training deck on Thursday.

Next: I'll schedule the training session with Operations for next Monday. That gives us the weekend to finalize everything. Sound good?
One thing: once Operations starts hiring, we need to monitor the process to make sure they're using the templates correctly. Should I check in with them mid-week to see how it's going?

Yes, good idea. I'll do a check-in with the Operations manager mid-week to see if there are any issues or questions. If there are blockers, we can address them quickly. I'll also ask them to flag any candidates who have accessibility needs so we can make sure we're handling those well.

For the onboarding side: once Operations makes offers, I'll make sure the new hires are set up in HRIS and payroll on time. I'll also send them the onboarding checklist so their manager knows what to do on day 1.

And I'll start collecting feedback from candidates and new hires once they're onboarded. I'll use a simple survey and a few interviews to understand their experience. Target: feedback collected by end of week 4.

Good. I'll also track any compliance issues or risks that come up during the pilot. If there are any problems with the templates or guidelines, I want to know immediately so we can adjust before full rollout.

So the pilot monitoring plan is:
- 441030: weekly check-in with Operations manager
- 167595: onboarding setup and checklist execution
- 549423: feedback collection from candidates and new hires
- 17956: compliance monitoring

Everyone reports back to me weekly. I'll consolidate into a pilot status report.

Perfect. Let me confirm the decisions:

D7: Pilot business unit is Operations. Timeline: 4 weeks starting next Monday. Three roles will be hired using the new process.

D8: Manager training plan approved. Training session scheduled for next Monday with Operations managers. Training deck includes process overview, templates walkthrough, compliance/anti-bias segment, and quick reference guide.

Everyone clear on their pilot responsibilities?
Clear. I'll have the training deck ready by Thursday for review. Then we deliver to Operations on Monday.

Alright, team. Pilot is locked in. Let's execute well and gather good feedback. I'll post a weekly pilot status update every Friday. Next update: Friday of next week with initial feedback from Operations.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot feedback, agree on adjustments, and confirm final rollout plan.

messages.text:
Hi team, I've compiled the pilot feedback summary (A7). Here's what we learned from the Operations pilot:

Positives:
- Job posting template was clear and attracted diverse candidates
- Interview scorecard helped managers make consistent decisions
- Onboarding checklist was practical and didn't overwhelm new hires
- Accessibility accommodations were handled smoothly

Areas for improvement:
- Managers found the anti-bias guideline too long; they want a one-page summary
- One candidate requested a written interview format instead of verbal; we didn't have a process for that
- The 90-day check-in timing conflicted with a business review cycle; need to align
- Payroll setup had a 2-day delay for one new hire; need to clarify HRIS touchpoints

Overall feedback: positive. Managers said the process was fair and transparent. New hires felt welcomed and supported.

I've documented all feedback and proposed changes. Let me know what you think.

Excellent summary. The feedback is constructive. Let me address the compliance and legal angles:

1. Anti-bias guideline: I'll create a one-page summary sheet that managers can reference, with the full guideline as a backup. That's a quick fix.

2. Written interview format: this is important for accessibility. I'll add a note to the guideline that managers should offer alternative interview formats (written, video, phone, etc.) if a candidate requests it. We need to be flexible here.

3. 90-day check-in timing: I'll coordinate with the business review cycle. We can shift the timing or align them. I'll check with the payroll team on this.

4. Payroll setup delay: I need to review the HRIS integration map with the payroll team. There might be a process gap we missed.

I'll have revised versions of A2 (anti-bias guideline) and A5 (KPI definition) ready by end of this week. Then we can move to D9 (agree on changes) and D10 (confirm go-live).

Good. The one-page summary for the anti-bias guideline is smart. Managers will actually use it if it's concise.

On the 90-day timing: I can check with Operations on how the business review cycle works and see if we can align. It might be as simple as shifting the check-in by a week or two.

On the payroll delay: I'll follow up with the payroll team too. There might be a manual step we can automate or clarify.

I'll also review the onboarding checklist based on the feedback. The 90-day timing issue affects the checklist, so I'll adjust it once we confirm the new timing. I'll also add a note about alternative interview formats so managers know to offer them.

Perfect. So the change list for D9 is:

1. Create one-page summary of anti-bias guideline
2. Add alternative interview format options to guideline
3. Align 90-day check-in timing with business review cycle
4. Clarify HRIS/payroll touchpoints to avoid setup delays
5. Update onboarding checklist with new timing

Once I have the revised documents and we've confirmed the payroll/HRIS fix, we'll lock in D9. Then D10 (confirm go-live date and governance model) will follow.
What about the KPI definition (A5)? Did the pilot give us any insights on what metrics matter most?

Good question. From the pilot, I'm seeing that time-to-hire is important, but so is candidate experience and diversity metrics. I'll refine A5 to include:

- Time-to-hire (days from posting to offer)
- Offer acceptance rate
- Diversity metrics (gender, disability, other demographics)
- 90-day retention
- Manager satisfaction with the process
- Candidate satisfaction (NPS or similar)

I'll have the updated A5 ready by end of week. We'll use this to track success after go-live.

Those metrics make sense. I'd add one more: manager time spent on hiring. If the new process takes significantly more time, we need to know that and adjust. But from the pilot, it didn't seem to add much overhead.

Good point. I'll add 'manager time per hire' to the KPI list. That's a practical metric that will help us understand the real cost of the process.

Alright, let me consolidate the post-pilot action plan:

1. 17956: revise A2 (anti-bias guideline with one-page summary), A3 (onboarding checklist with new timing), A5 (KPI definition with expanded metrics), and coordinate with payroll on HRIS fix. Ready by end of week.

2. 441030: confirm 90-day timing with Operations and payroll team. Ready by end of week.

3. 549423: finalize feedback summary and any additional insights. Ready by end of week.

4. 167595: update onboarding checklist based on timing changes. Ready by end of week.

Once all revisions are done, we'll lock in D9 (agree on changes) and D10 (confirm go-live). Target: final approval by next Tuesday, go-live by day 28 of the project.

I've also finalized the escalation path (A8, T11). It documents common issues (template questions, accommodation requests, payroll delays, etc.) and who to contact for each. I'll share it with the team for review by end of week.

Great. The escalation path is important for rollout. Once we go live, HR staff and managers need to know who to contact for different issues. I'll review your draft and we'll finalize it as part of the governance model (T12).

Alright, team. Let's lock in the final decisions:

D9: Framework changes based on pilot feedback are approved. Changes include: one-page anti-bias summary, alternative interview formats, aligned 90-day timing, clarified HRIS/payroll touchpoints, and expanded KPI metrics.

D10: Go-live date is confirmed for day 28 of the project (one week from today). Governance model includes: escalation path (A8), review cycle (quarterly), change log process, and ownership assignments.

Once everyone confirms these decisions, we're ready to roll out the framework to all business units. Final communication and training will happen next week.

Confirmed. D9 and D10 are locked. I'll coordinate the rollout communication with all business units next week. We'll send the updated templates, guidelines, and training materials to all managers by day 27. Go-live is day 28.

Perfect. Project is on track. All deliverables are complete and approved. Pilot feedback has been incorporated. Framework is ready for rollout.

Post-go-live, we'll monitor KPIs (A5), track escalations (A8), and conduct a quarterly review to identify improvements. I'll schedule a post-rollout retrospective for week 6 to capture lessons learned.

Great work, team. Let's execute the rollout flawlessly.
